02

Server

Choose a VPS

A VPS is a small computer in a data center. It runs continuously, so your Telegram terminal remains available when your own PC is off.

Operating systemUbuntu 24.04 LTS22.04 LTS is also supported
Comfortable starting point1 vCPU · 2 GB RAM10+ GB storage
NetworkPublic IPv4Outbound HTTPS + SSH access

These are conservative starting specifications, not a measured minimum. Final resource usage should be benchmarked after the public release.

1

Create the server

Select Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (or 22.04 LTS) and a nearby region.

2

Save the access details

Copy the server IP, SSH username and password or private key.

3

Protect the account

Enable two-factor authentication with your VPS provider.

03

Remote access

Connect with MobaXterm

On Windows, MobaXterm provides a simple SSH window. Download it only from the official website.

Official downloadmobaxterm.mobatek.net ↗
1

Create a session

Open Session → SSH.

2

Enter the server address

Use the public IP from your VPS provider. Keep port 22 unless your provider specifies another.

3

Set the username

Usually root or ubuntu. Your provider will tell you which one applies.

4

Verify and sign in

Confirm the host fingerprint against your provider's control panel, then use the supplied password or SSH key.

Do not ignore a changed host fingerprint.

If the warning appears unexpectedly, stop and verify the server identity with your VPS provider before connecting.

04

Credentials

Create your Telegram bot

Your bot is created through Telegram's official @BotFather. The token it gives you is effectively the password for controlling that bot.

Open in Telegram@BotFather ↗
1

Start BotFather

Check that the username is exactly @BotFather and that it is verified.

2

Send /newbot

Choose a display name and a unique username ending in bot.

3

Copy the token

Save it temporarily in a private password manager. The installer will ask for it once.

4

Find your numeric user ID

The allowed user ID is a number, not your @username. Verify it carefully before saving the private configuration.

05

Credentials

Create a Polyester API key

Create a dedicated key for the bot. Polyester uses an Ed25519 keypair: the public key is registered with your account while the private key stays on your server and signs requests locally.

Installer needsAPI Key IDak_…
Installer needsPrivate key seed32-byte hex secret
Installer does not needPublic keyAlready registered in Polyester

Recommended policy

PermissionLevelWhy
BalancesReadPortfolio display
Spot tradingRead + WriteOrders and fills
TransfersNoneNot used by the bot
WithdrawalsNoneNot used by the bot
Best practice:

Use a dedicated key, set an expiry date and, when your host has a stable public IP, allowlist it as YOUR_PUBLIC_IP/32. Never grant withdrawal or transfer permissions.

API key guide ↗ Authentication docs ↗

Deployment

Install the terminal

Choose your setup first

The installation steps depend on where the bot will run.

Choose VPS or local →
Selected pathVPS · UbuntuChange

This command downloads the public repository and opens an interactive setup wizard directly inside your SSH session.

Ubuntu terminalOne-line guided installer
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/web3cadet/polyester-community-trading-bot/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --repo https://github.com/web3cadet/polyester-community-trading-bot.git
Review before running.

The command reads install.sh from GitHub ↗. Inspect remote scripts before piping them into a shell.

The installer will ask for

  1. 01
    Risk acknowledgement

    Confirms that this is testnet software.

  2. 02
    Telegram credentials

    Bot token and allowed numeric user ID.

  3. 03
    Polyester credentials

    API Key ID and private signing seed.

  4. 04
    Validation and launch

    Builds the container, checks read access and starts the bot.

Secrets are written to the VPS .env file with restricted permissions. They are not sent to a shared bot operator.

Selected pathLocal · WindowsChange

Create an empty folder, open that folder in VS Code, open the integrated terminal and paste one command. The installer handles the repository, dependencies, validation, private configuration and first launch.

VS Code terminal · WindowsOne-line guided installer
npx --yes github:web3cadet/polyester-community-trading-bot
Runs from the public source.

Review the repository on GitHub ↗ before launching the guided installer.

What happens automatically

  1. 01
    Download or update

    Copies the current public release into the open folder while preserving .env and local data.

  2. 02
    Private setup wizard

    Asks for the Telegram token, allowed ID, API Key ID and private signing seed. Secret input is hidden.

  3. 03
    Install and verify

    Synchronizes dependencies, runs type checks and tests, builds production code and validates the Polyester API policy.

  4. 04
    Launch and open

    Shows a green progress bar, starts the bot in the background and prints its direct t.me link.

Nothing else to edit.

After the final confirmation the installer creates the protected local .env, checks a non-mutating live order preview and launches the full LIVE testnet terminal.

Re-running the same one-line command updates the application and dependencies while preserving credentials and SQLite data. The bot still stops if Windows shuts down or sleeps; choose the VPS path for continuous availability.

10

Non-negotiables

Security

✓

Use a dedicated API key

Do not reuse a key from another app or environment.

✓

Keep permissions minimal

Balances and spot trading only. No transfers or withdrawals.

✓

Restrict access

One allowed Telegram ID and, where possible, one VPS IP.

✓

Keep secrets off-screen

Never share .env, tokens, private keys or logs containing them.

✓

Keep the host updated

Apply operating-system, Node.js and dependency security updates.

✓

Rotate after exposure

Revoke compromised credentials first; do not merely delete a message.

11

Common problems

Troubleshooting

api_key_policy_required+

The API key exists, but the required policy is missing. In Polyester, attach balance read and spot trading permissions, save, then restart the bot.

TIMESTAMP_SKEW+

The VPS clock differs too much from the API. Enable automatic time synchronization, verify the clock, then retry.

SIGNATURE_INVALID+

The Key ID and private signing seed do not belong to the same API key, or the secret was copied incorrectly. Reconfigure both values together.

IP_NOT_ALLOWED+

The key's IP allowlist does not include the VPS public IP. Add the exact server address as /32 or correct the existing entry.

Balances are empty or incomplete+

Check whether assets are in the trading account rather than the funding account, and confirm the key has balance-read permission.

The bot does not answer+

Confirm that your numeric Telegram ID is allowed, then open ./manage.sh and check Status and Logs.

12

Short answers

Frequently asked questions

Is this a mainnet bot?

No. The current build and this guide are for Polyester testnet.

Is it an official Polyester product?

No. It is an independent, community-built open-source interface.

Does the installer need my public key?

No. It needs the ak_… Key ID and matching private signing seed. The public key is already registered in Polyester.

Can I run it on my own PC?

Yes, but it stops when the PC sleeps or disconnects. A VPS is better for continuous access.

Does the developer receive my keys?

No. In the self-hosted model, credentials stay in the local server configuration you control.

Can the bot withdraw funds?

It is not designed to. Do not grant withdrawal or transfer permissions.
